statement: Kernel-checked classical mixed-power cancellation; advisory statement coverage pending. Let S be a finite index set, p_i distinct positive noninteger real exponents, and c_i real coefficients with at least one nonzero. For every real A>0 and B, the averages (1/N)*sum_(n<N) exp(2*pi*i*sum_(i in S) c_i*(A*n+B)^p_i) tend to zero. The main proof removes zero coefficients and chooses the largest remaining exponent. More generally, it suffices that a unique largest exponent lies strictly between some natural m and m+1 and has nonzero coefficient; lower exponents may be arbitrary real numbers. A derivative tower with D_0=f, a_0=c, a_(k+1)=a_k*(p-k), eventual derivative D_k'=D_(k+1), and D_k(x)/x^(p-k) tending to a_k gives cancellation when c!=0 and m<p<m+1. Actual positive fixed differences preserve this tower with exponent p-1 and leading coefficient h*c*p, proved using moving mean-value points. The base case follows from the proved first-derivative estimate, finite-prefix removal, and conjugation; higher orders follow by qualitative van der Corput. Real powers, finite addition, lower-order terms and positive affine progression changes are proved to satisfy the tower conditions. No cancellation, equidistribution, or analytic estimate is assumed in the concrete mixed-power theorem. This does not yet prove Fourier-to-box recurrence, the concrete Paper E exponent/box specialization, shrinking-target bounds, or termination.
